title: In the wheel, a cash-secured put and a covered call are the same trade
summary: A cash-secured put and a covered call at the same strike and expiry have the same payoff, maximum loss and maximum profit. This follows from put-call parity. The wheel looks like two trades only because people strike puts below and calls above the stock price.

steps.caption: The stock trades at $100. We compare a short $100 put with 100 shares plus a short $100 call.
Line A: the cash-secured put. Gain capped at the premium, loss grows as the stock falls.
Line B: the covered call. It lies on top of line A: same max profit, same max loss.
The difference is near zero, only carry. Put-call parity makes them one economic trade.
Most traders strike the put below and the call above the price. That is only a strike choice.

takeaways: A cash-secured put and a covered call at the same strike have the same payoff at expiry.
The wheel is one economic exposure, not two different trades.
Differences come from where you choose to strike each leg.
caveats: Small differences remain from dividends, interest and early assignment.
